title: WebNavigator: Global Web Navigation via Interaction Graph Retrieval
claim: A two-phase system builds a global map of the environment offline, then retrieves, reasons over and jumps along it online.
layout: 3 stacked bands, left-to-right flow, browser-window frames, numbered steps
description: The figure is a wide, three-band pipeline diagram with a title for each phase. The top band, Phase I (offline), has two browser-window panels in purple. The first shows website logos, an arrow labeled Exploration, a node-edge Interaction Graph, and a dashed callout listing a screenshot, DOM structure and accessibility tree. The second shows stacked page screenshots, an Embedding arrow and a vector database icon. The middle band, Phase II (online), starts with a purple strip, navigate(domain, query), with three numbered steps: Recall, Reason, Teleport. Below it, blue panels show Recall (query, vector database, top-K candidate screenshots with scores) and Reason (intent plus candidates fed to a selector, with an LLM rationale). The bottom yellow band shows Teleport, with path finding on the graph and a chain of screenshots joined by actions a1–a3 to the target page. Hatched blue arrows carry the flow.
caption: Overview of WebNavigator. WebNavigator resolves Topological Blindness via a twophase paradigm. (1) Offline Interaction Graph Construction. A heuristic auto-exploration engine discovers dynamic page observations at zero-token cost and indexes all observations into a vector database. (2) Online Retrieval-Augmented Navigation. The Global-View Navigator implements a three-stage workflow: Retrieve top-k candidates from the Interaction Graph via multimodal retrieval; Reason to identify the optimal target page; and Teleport by computing and executing the shortest path within the Interaction Graph, achieving globally optimal navigation.
abstract: Despite significant advances in autonomous web navigation, current methods remain far from human-level performance in complex web environments. We argue that this limitation stems from Topological Blindness, where agents are forced to explore via trial-and-error without access to the global topological structure of the environment. To overcome this limitation, we introduce WebNavigator, which reframes web navigation from probabilistic exploration into deterministic retrieval and pathfinding. WebNavigator constructs Interaction Graphs via zero-token cost heuristic exploration offline and implements a Retrieve-Reason-Teleport workflow for global navigation online. WebNavigator achieves state-of-the-art performance on WebArena and OnlineMind2Web. On WebArena multi-site tasks, WebNavigator achieves a 72.9\% success rate, more than doubling the performance of enterprise-level agents. This work reveals that Topological Blindness, rather than model reasoning capabilities alone, is an underestimated bottleneck in autonomous web navigation.
